figures.caption: Figure 2. Subject settings and diagnostic comparisons. (a) Within-subject (WS) trains and tests on the same participant. Joint trains one model on all ten participants and tests each separately. Strict leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) trains on nine participants and tests the held-out participant without target calibration. All three settings use unseen test concepts. (b) Diagnostics compare correct and matched-wrong EEG, averages of few and many test trials, and random and hard galleries of equal size.

Figure 3. Subject-wise retrieval for 13 systems. Markers show mean Top-1 over three training seeds at fixed S01–S10 angles. Radial bars show ±1 seed SD. Linear radial ranges are 0–70% (WS), 0–60% (Joint), and 0–22% (strict LOSO). The LOSO panel is enlarged, so compare scores using the tick labels. Table 1 gives the exact values in columns S01–S10.

Figure 4. Joint retrieval examples. Each row shows one subject–query pair. Six distinct concepts are sampled from 2,000 pairs across ten subjects without conditioning on retrieval results. The left column shows ground truth (GT). AlignVis, Visual Blur, and NICE are ranked first, seventh, and thirteenth by mean Joint Top-1 among 13 methods. The top five images use archived seed-0 scores. Green borders mark GT wherever it appears.

Figure 5. Target access and visual configuration. (a) Left labels give frozen strict-LOSO Top-1 (%, mean ± subject SD). Points show subject-paired gains over frozen inference (pp) with descriptive 95% intervals. Unlabeled calibration uses four repeats per stimulus in an independent cohort (I4) or four or 80 repeats in the test cohort (T4/T80). Only iTransformer uses SATTC, with T80 input. (b,c) Points and bars give Top-1 mean ± subject SD for RN50, L/14, and H/14 under WS and strict LOSO. Colors follow (a). The 512-dimensional PCA is fitted on training images only.

Table 2. Paired Top-1 gains over EEG controls. Correct-minus-zero (∆Zero) and correct-minus-matched-wrong (∆Matched) gains are in percentage points. Each entry gives mean ± SD across ten subjects after averaging three training seeds per subject. Both controls share the checkpoint, queries, and gallery with the correct condition. Matched-wrong EEG comes from a different stimulus with the same participant, session composition, and repeat count. Zero EEG is an out-of-distribution diagnostic. In each column, bold marks the highest mean gain and underlining marks the second-highest. Gains use the original paired runs.

Figure 6. Data requirements. Curves show subject-macro Top-1 means (%). (a) Test-trial averaging with fixed checkpoints. (b) Candidate count K, with chance at 100/K (dotted gray). At K = 10, vertical lines connect random and hard galleries. Hard-gallery results use × for WS and + for LOSO. Solid and dashed curves in (a,b) denote WS and LOSO. (c) Training images retained per concept (solid Joint, dashed LOSO). Nominal 25% retains three of ten images, so it is plotted at 30%. (d) Number of LOSO source subjects, using all available data (solid) or matching sample and update counts (dashed). Panels (c,d) show NICE-BASE, ATM, and BrainFLORA uni.

Figure 7. Robustness and calibration. (a) Heatmap values give the ratio of perturbed to clean WS subject-macro Top-1, in percent. At 100%, accuracy matches the clean baseline. Noise, channel dropout, and gain are applied after 80-trial averaging. (b) Colors identify methods. Open and filled markers give native and temperature-scaled expected calibration error (ECE, lower is better) under WS and LOSO. Scaling uses temperatures fitted on source validation data and preserves within-query ranks. Figure 5(a) describes calibration with unlabeled target EEG.
